quote: Man hat also nach Hülfssatz 3 2 ganze zu 2 prime Zahlen $\pi, \kappa$ in $k$ so zu bestimmen, dass für alle Primideale $\mathfrak{w}$ in $k$ gleichzeitig
english: So, by Lemma 3, one has to determine 2 integers π, κ in k, prime to 2, such that for all prime ideals w in k simultaneously [conditions (1)] hold and moreover π, κ have prescribed signs in the real fields conjugate to k.
topic: Hilbert reduces the solvability of a ternary quadratic (norm) equation over a number field k to finding two integers π, κ satisfying conditions on Hilbert norm residue symbols at all prime ideals, using auxiliary lemmas (Hilfssätze) 1–3 and an auxiliary prime l.

triage.modern_statement: This is one step in proving that a ternary quadratic form over a number field k has a nontrivial solution, i.e. the 'norm equation' question: is c a norm from k(√a)/k, or equivalently does a x² + b y² = z² have a solution in k? In the note, Hilbert uses his Lemma 3 to reduce the problem to an existence statement. One must find two integers π, κ in k, prime to 2, such that the quadratic Hilbert norm-residue symbols involving π and κ take prescribed values at every prime ideal w of k, and π, κ have prescribed signs at the real embeddings of k. In modern terms this is the existence part of the theory of Hilbert symbols: values at each place can be realized by global elements when they satisfy the product formula (Hilbert reciprocity). That fact is what drives the local–global principle (Hasse–Minkowski) for quadratic forms over number fields. The exact conditions (1) and the lemmas are not given in the excerpt, so their precise form cannot be checked.
triage.answered_by: This is part of Hilbert's own program on relative quadratic fields and quadratic forms with algebraic coefficients, which he posed in 1900 as his 11th problem. The general local–global principle for quadratic forms over arbitrary number fields was proved by Helmut Hasse in papers of 1923–1924 (the Hasse–Minkowski theorem), which settles the solvability question in general. Hilbert's product formula for the norm-residue symbol is the reciprocity law behind it.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's 11th problem (ICM 1900) asks for the theory of quadratic forms with any algebraic number coefficients. It extends what Minkowski did for rational coefficients and is summarized as 'classify quadratic forms over algebraic number fields'. Hasse published his work on it in 1923 and 1924, which led to the Hasse principle and the Hasse–Minkowski theorem.
In 1923–1924 Hasse proved the Hasse principle for quadratic forms over any number field k.
Hasse generalized Minkowski's result to arbitrary number fields in 1924 (the Hasse–Minkowski theorem).
Hilbert discovered the product formula for the norm-residue symbol, the reciprocity law that governs which local symbol values can occur globally.

The local–global principle over number fields goes back to the generalization of quadratic reciprocity by Hilbert and Furtwängler, with further local–global principles following class field theory after 1923.
